XXIIII.}}</noinclude>the floud came, and tooke them al: so also shal the comming of the Sonne of man be. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=40}}† Then two shal be in the field: one shal be taken, and one shal be left. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=41}}† tvvo vvomen grinding in the mill: one shal be taken, and one shal be left. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=42}}† Watch therfore because you knovv not vvhat houre your Lord vvil come. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=43}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for a Cōfessor that is a Bishop. And for S. Clement martyr, Nouemb. 23.}}But this knovv ye, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Thes. 5, 1.''}}* if the good man of the house did knovv vvhat houre the theefe vvould come, he vvould surely vvatch, and vvould not suffer his house to be broken vp. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=44}}† Therfore be you also ready, because at vvhat houre you knovv not, the Sonne of man vvil come.

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=45}}† Who, thinkest thou, is a faithful and vvise seruant, vvhom his lord hath appointed ouer his familie, to giue them meate in season? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=46}}† Blessed is that seruant, vvhom vvhen his lord commeth, he shal finde so doing. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=47}}† Amen I say to you, that ouer al his goods shal he appoint him.⊣ {{verse|chapter=24|verse=48}}† But if that naughtie seruant shal say in his hart, My lord is long a comming: {{verse|chapter=24|verse=49}}† and shal beginne to strike his felovv-seruants, and eateth, and drinketh vvith drunkards: {{verse|chapter=24|verse=50}}† the lord of that seruant shal come in a day that he hopeth not, and an houre that he knovveth not, {{verse|chapter=24|verse=51}}† and shal deuide him, and appoint his portion vvith the hypocrites: there shal be vveeping and gnashing of teeth.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XXIIII.}}}}

''2. Not left.''] This was fulfilled 40 yeres after Christes Ascension by Vespasian the Emperour and his sonne Titus. ''Euseb. li. 3. c. 6 & seq. ex Iosepho''. Vpon which wordes, ''There shal not be left &c'', which threaten the destruction of the Iewes Temple: and those wordes, ''Vpon this Rocke I wil build my Church'', {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 16.''}}which promise the building of the Catholike Church of al nations: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Church can neuer faile.}}S. Chrysostome {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Li. adu. Gentes quod Christus sit Deus, prope finem''.}}making a long comparison of these two prophecies of Christ, saith thus: Thou seest in both, his great and vnspeakable power, in that that he increased and built vp them that worshipped him, and those that stumbled at him, he abased, destroyed, and plucked them vp by the roote. Doest thou see how whatsoeuer he hath built, no man shal destroy: and whatsoeuer he hath destroyed, no man shal build? He builded the Church, and no man shal be able to destroy it: he destroyed the Temple, and no man is able to build it, and that in so long time. For they haue endeuoured both to destroy that, and could not: and they haue attempted to build vp this, and they could not doe that neither. &c.

''3. The signe.''] Our Maister knowing that it was not profitable nor seemly for them to know these secretes, gaue them by way of Prophecie, warning of diuerse miseries, signes, and tokens, that should fall, some further of, and some neerer the later day: by which the faithful might alwayes prepare them selues, but neuer be certaine of the houre, day, moneth, nor yere, when it should fall. ''Aug. Ep.80''.

''4. Seduce.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Heretikes seduce vnder faire titles.}}The first and principal warning, needful for the faithful from Christes Ascension to the very end of the world, is, that they be not deceaued by Heretikes, which vnder the titles of true teachers and the name of Christ and his Gospel, wil seduce many.

''5. I am Christ.''] Not only such as haue named them selues Christ, as Simon, Menander, and such like: but al Arch-heretikes be Christes to their folowers, Luther to the Lutherans, Caluin to the Caluinists: because they beleeue them, rather then Christ speaking in his Church.<noinclude>{{rh|||''12. Iniquity}}</noinclude>
